scope: Microbenchmark only; not battle throughput or qualification. Ten million cached native calls per function; operands binary64 numbers; full call_value dispatch retained. Shared cloud-host timing is noisy; sqrt has no demonstrated improvement.
benchmarkRustSource:
use js_runtime::{Runtime,Value};use std::{hint::black_box,time::Instant};
fn main(){let mut rt=Runtime::new();let global=Value::Object(rt.global_object);let k=rt.string("Math");let math=rt.get(global,k).unwrap();for name in["sqrt","min","max"]{let k=rt.string(name);let f=rt.get(math,k).unwrap();let args=[Value::Number(1.23456789),Value::Number(-0.0)];let start=Instant::now();for _ in 0..10000000{black_box(rt.call_value(black_box(f),math,black_box(&args)).unwrap());}println!("{} {}",name,start.elapsed().as_nanos());}}
invariants: Only Value::Number bypasses generic ToNumber; every other value executes unchanged conversion.
Argument traversal and conversion remain left-to-right, including all arguments after NaN.
Same js_math min/max operations retain signed zero and NaN payload policy.
Writable Math properties still resolve and dispatch normally; no compiler intrinsic substitution.
